candidate.answerReason: The 600-gram batch contains 411 calories. A 200-gram serving is one third of the batch and therefore contains 137 calories.

methods.label: Take the serving's fraction of the batch
methods.explanation:
First find the mass and calories of the whole batch. Its mass is
\[
100+100+400=600\text{ grams}.
\]
The lemon juice contributes \(25\) calories, the sugar contributes \(386\), and the water contributes none, for a total of
\[
25+386=411\text{ calories}.
\]
For the same mixed lemonade, calories are proportional to serving mass. A \(200\)-gram serving is \(200/600=\tfrac13\) of the batch, so it contains
\[
411\cdot\frac13=\boxed{137}
\]
calories, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Adding ingredient totals and scaling by a simple fraction provides a complete elementary proportional-reasoning solution.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is applying proportional reasoning to a serving of a mixture. Direct proportion and the meaning of a fraction support taking the same fraction of the total calories as of the batch mass. Fraction multiplication is explicitly used by this route. Inverse proportion and a cross-multiplication algorithm are unnecessary.
